data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Silver salt — antiseptic, astringent, caustic

## Mechanism of action
- Silver ions precipitate proteins → antiseptic and astringent at low concentration, caustic (chemical cautery) at high concentration

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Stick: haemostasis after shave/punch biopsy, excess granulation tissue (hypergranulation), pyogenic granuloma (small), umbilical granuloma, warts (adjunct)
- 0.5% solution: wet dressings for burns and weeping lesions; ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis (historic, 1%)

## Dose & formulations
- Touch the moistened stick to the area for a few seconds; protect surrounding skin

## Adverse effects
- Black/brown staining of skin (silver deposition), local pain, argyria with chronic use; hyponatraemia with large-area wet dressings

## Contraindications
- Large areas; eyes (stick)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Chemical haemostasis and hypergranulation; black staining

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Silver nitrate) and ch.13 (Topical haemostatic agents). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
